cases.label: Double-negative charging trap
cases.trap_explained: Contains the words 'charging' and a negation ('don't skip'), which a naive keyword matcher reads as a no_charge_window. Semantically it means the OPPOSITE: charging should continue normally. Correct answer is no_op.

operator_notes: Don't skip the normal charging routine this morning, everything is running fine there.
Keep at least 60 kWh in reserve from 7 PM until 9 PM in case of a brief outage.

expected_directive_interpretation.why: Double negative ('don't skip') means charging proceeds as normal.

cases.label: Negation-of-negation discharge trap
cases.trap_explained: 'No need to prevent discharging' double negative = discharge UNRESTRICTED.

operator_notes: There's no need to prevent the battery from discharging tonight; operations are normal.
The IT helpdesk will be closed for a training session next Thursday.

cases.label: Redundant paraphrase of the same directive
cases.trap_explained: Two notes SAME solar directive, opposite phrasing. Both applies=true factor=0.3.

operator_notes: Only about 30% of the forecast solar will be usable from 9 AM until 11 AM due to haze.
That same 9-to-11 AM window will see roughly a 70% drop in solar output.
Maintain at least a quarter of the battery's capacity in reserve from 5 PM to 7 PM.
Keep at least three-quarters of total battery capacity available from 6 PM to 10 PM for a planned outage drill.

cases.label: Non-contiguous solar_reduction window
cases.trap_explained: TWO sessions in ONE note -> [7,13] factor 0.4

operator_notes: Panel cleaning happens twice today: once from 7 to 8 AM and again from 1 to 2 PM. Both times cut usable solar to about 40% of forecast.
Grid intake during the 6 to 8 PM window should not pass 190,000 watt-hours in any single hour.
Do not charge the battery from 11 PM until 1 AM for a nightly relay test.

cases.label: Vague magnitude, no number stated
